slides.title: The two clocks
slides.source: Source: Chapter 1, “Scripts and the two clocks”; Chapter 4, “Two clocks”; glossary, Scenes, nodes and signals.
slides.notes: Counts are computed: floor(0.25 x fps). Step 3: 4 px per frame against 240 px/s scaled by 1/fps.

new_texts: Runs once per rendered frame; the rate varies by machine.
30 fps gives 7 frames in 0.25 s, 144 fps gives 36. The count depends on the machine.
all_texts: Runs once per rendered frame; the rate varies by machine.

→ Bind Space to the action jump; test is_action_just_pressed("jump") each tick
“tell the main scene when the player dies”
→ Player emits hit; connect it to Main.game_over; do not poll
“show me what the game really contains”
→ Run it, switch the Scene dock to Remote, and count: 13 nodes, not 1

slides.title: Before you trust a Godot change
slides.picture: A checklist of six items drawn one at a time.

new_texts: Does the saved scene match the running tree? Check the Scene dock's Remote tab.
Does movement that must repeat run in _physics_process, on the fixed tick?
Is the input an action in the Input Map, and do I want just-pressed or held?
Who emits, who connects, and should this be a signal instead of a poll?
Do layer and mask use the value 2^(n−1), and does the shape match the art?
Is the area's overlap a tick old, and is the shared number in one resource?
Then say it exactly: not “make it collide”, but “layer 2, mask 3”.
